batchId: DC research batch 01 (queue order: Alfred Pennyworth to Batman)
method: Web research against encyclopedic and issue-index pages. Every feat names the issue or storyline the cited page gives. Claims the cited page did not support were left out or listed under unknowns. No numeric tiers, no win probabilities. All records stay provisional until a different contributor checks the cited support.
baselineContinuity: Mainline DC Comics, matching data/pool-lore-dc.js. Films, animation, games and Elseworlds are excluded unless named.

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics, Golden Age (Batman #16, 1943) through Rebirth; dead in primary continuity since Batman vol. 3 #77 (2019)
characters.summary: The Wayne family butler is a trained ex-soldier, medic, actor and intelligence hand. He fights only as an ordinary older man and is mostly a support and logistics piece, not a frontline combatant.

techniques: armed and unarmed combat (below Bruce Wayne's level)
shotgun, the one firearm Batman tolerates him carrying

mechanisms: deception and avoidance rather than toughness

support: Field medicine: suturing, bullet removal, arthroscopy
Maintains and builds Batcave technology including the Batcomputer

feats.claim: Fought two slavers on his own during No Man's Land before Batman rescued him.
Escaped a cell and knocked out Hush.
Tricked Bane into helping him reach an emergency cave under Arkham, where he called for help.
Shot down the Batwing with Batman flying it, under Two-Face's blackmail.

notableResults.opponent: Bane (acting for the Flashpoint Thomas Wayne)
notableResults.note: Held hostage, then Bane broke his neck.

weaknesses: Ordinary older human with no superhuman durability
His medical skill was not enough for Batman's broken back (Knightfall) or skull fracture (Hush)
unknowns: His service branch and role (special forces, intelligence, medic) changes between retellings, so no single military rank is treated as canon here.

sources.supports: Abilities (combat below Bruce's level, shotgun, medic, intelligence, acting), LotDK #118, Batman Eternal #31 and #47, All-Star Batman #11, death in Batman vol. 3 #77
His military job (medic, commando, special forces) is rarely consistent across versions

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics from Legends #1 (1986); New 52 redesign (young and thin) reverted in Rebirth
characters.summary: Waller has no powers. Her threat is command: she runs Task Force X, holds kill switches on its members and uses political leverage. Her personal combat is listed in references but has no documented winning fight.

techniques: command of Task Force X (Suicide Squad)
detonation authority over squad members' implanted explosives
offense.range: strategic and remote through subordinates; short range in person

mechanisms: operates through subordinates and contingencies rather than in person

conditional.ability: Direct control of Chemo during a mission
conditional.dependsOn: Nanotechnology implanted in her (Checkmate vol. 2 #20, Salvation Run)

conditional.ability: Kryptonite stockpile and the AAB creature

feats.claim: Appointed the White Queen of Checkmate by the UN.
Faked her own death with Deadshot and Enchantress.
Persuaded the President to keep Task Force X and put Rick Flag in charge.

notableResults.note: Apparently shot dead; the death was a setup she arranged.

weaknesses: Ordinary human
No documented one-on-one fight win (the cited page describes none)
unknowns: How well her listed martial arts and marksmanship hold up against trained fighters has no sourced fight.

sources.supports: Non-powered; strategist, martial artist, markswoman; explosive implants; Chemo nanotech (Checkmate vol. 2 #20); Checkmate #6; Superman/Batman #44-49; Suicide Squad (2016) #11-15; Rebirth; no physical fight win described
Publisher profile: founder of Task Force X; lists combat strategy, combat skill and political influence

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics: Crisis on Infinite Earths (1985-86), Sinestro Corps War (Green Lantern vol. 4, 2007), Blackest Night (2009-10), Darkseid War (Justice League vol. 2 #44-49, 2015-16)
characters.summary: A cosmic antimatter tyrant who consumed universes during the original Crisis. He is enormously durable and is rebuilt by the antimatter universe when destroyed, but every major defeat came from many heroes combining their power.

techniques: using the Black Racer through the Anti-Life Equation (Darkseid War)

mechanisms: rebuilt by the antimatter universe if destroyed while that universe exists
Life Shell armor holding in his leaking life force

feats.claim: Killed Supergirl (Kara Zor-El), who sacrificed herself to save Superman.
Killed two Green Lanterns and injured a Daxamite Lantern.
Used the Black Racer, enslaved through the Anti-Life Equation, to kill Darkseid.
Powered the Black Lantern Central Battery because Nekron could not fully control him.

notableResults.opponent: Doctor Light, Alexander Luthor Jr., Darkseid, Superboy-Prime and Kal-L together
notableResults.note: Weakened by the group; Kal-L finished him by punching him into a star.
Barry destroyed the antimatter cannon at the cost of his life.

notableResults.opponent: Superboy-Prime, after John Stewart and Guy Gardner dropped New Warworld on him
notableResults.note: Superboy-Prime flew through his chest and threw his body into space.

notableResults.opponent: Steve Trevor holding the Anti-Life Equation (given by Grail)

weaknesses: Life force leaks without the Life Shell armor, leaving him unstable
Repeatedly beaten by combined assaults
Anti-Life Equation wielded against him
unknowns: No single sourced statement of his top speed or reaction time.
How much of the universe-consuming scale applies in a single arena fight is not established.

sources.supports: Powers list, Crisis #7, #8 and #12 events, GL vol. 4 #25, Blackest Night #7-8, Justice League vol. 2 #44-49, Life Shell and regeneration limits (Wikipedia offline copy, Oct 2023)
Publisher profile: caused the Crisis on Infinite Earths; destroyer of universes

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics Orin/Arthur Curry across eras. Excludes the Lady of the Lake water hand (separate form) and film versions.
characters.summary: Atlantean king with superhuman strength, deep-sea durability and worldwide command of sea life. He is far stronger in water than on land, and dehydration erodes his strength over time.

techniques: telepathic command and summoning of sea life worldwide through the Clear
harpoon/hook prosthetic (1990s era): fires on a line, spins like a drill, psionically controlled STAR Labs model
offense.range: melee; sea-life summons at long range near water

mechanisms: superhuman durability built for crushing ocean depths

mobility: Echolocation after Poseidon opened his link to the Clear (blinded era)

conditional.dependsOn: Which trident he carries varies by era; not assumed for every version

feats.claim: Fought Poseidon's son Triton for control of the ocean and won, then received part of a sea god's power.
feats.citation: 1990s Aquaman series (issue not given by the cited pages)

notableResults.note: One source says Triton let him win; treat as a contested win.

weaknesses: Dehydration: strength and endurance fall the longer he is out of water
The out-of-water limit varies by era: one hour pre-Crisis, later uncertain and dependent on air moisture
Marine command mainly works on sea life
unknowns: Issue numbers for the Triton fight and the hook's introduction were not confirmed in this pass.

sources.supports: Publisher profile: super strength, durability, control over sea life, exceptional swimming, underwater breathing
1990s profile: dehydration limit (one hour pre-Crisis, later uncertain), harpoon/hook functions, marine-only control limits, Triton fight with Triton letting him win
The Clear, worldwide sea-life command, echolocation after blindness, STAR Labs psionic hook, Triton fight and sea-god power
Prime Earth weakness: strength and endurance diminish the longer he is out of the water

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics, Aquaman (2003) series by Rick Veitch and successors, where the Lady of the Lake gives Orin the Hand of the Waterbearer
characters.formDifferences: Same Orin with the same Atlantean body, but the harpoon is replaced by a hand of living water from the Secret Sea. The hand adds healing by touch, changing water density, pulling moisture out of objects, scrying, negating magic, controlling water and crossing dimensions, and it can act on its own. Violent use hurts the bearer. The harpoon's line and drill tricks do not carry over.
characters.summary: Aquaman as the Waterbearer: a mystic water hand turns him into a healer and water-shaper with anti-magic tools, at a real cost whenever the hand is used violently.

techniques: base Atlantean strength and sea-life command
offense.range: melee to short range; dimensional travel

feats.claim: Learns the hand can change water density, draw moisture out of objects and heal; heals the Necromonstrocity and Rodunn with a touch.

weaknesses: Violent use or the death touch causes the bearer great pain and could kill him
Heavy violent use summons the Thirst, which attacks the Secret Sea (Comic Vine says Orin later defeated it)
Inherits base dehydration limits
unknowns: Whether the hand stops the dehydration weakness is not stated in the cited pages.
Combat feats using the hand offensively were not confirmed in this pass.

sources.supports: Aquaman (2003) #3, Rick Veitch, Feb 2003: water density, moisture drawing, healing touch; Lady of the Lake's explanation
Hand of the Waterbearer: enhances abilities, healing, density change, scrying, magic negation, water manipulation, dimension travel, independent action; violent-use pain and the Thirst
Series identity: Aquaman (2003-2006), Lady of the Lake gives him a magical water hand with healing power

characters.continuity: Mainline post-Crisis DC Comics from Wonder Woman vol. 2 #1 (1987). The New 52 'War' (Wonder Woman vol. 4) is an older mentor figure who dies in vol. 4 #23, and Rebirth has him imprisoned on Themyscira; those differences are noted, not merged.
characters.summary: The Olympian god of war: immortal, armored, strengthened and healed by violence and able to command any weapon. His power rises with conflict, and he can be outmaneuvered when war would leave him with no one to rule.

techniques: telekinetic command of any weapon or armor
necromancy and undead armies (as God of the Dead)

mechanisms: reported to be harmable only by magical weapons

feats.claim: Grew strong enough during the Cold War escalation that the other gods and the Amazons neared death.
Became God of the Dead after Hades abandoned the role (post-Crisis).
feats.citation: Post-Crisis Wonder Woman (issue not given by the cited page)

notableResults.note: Bound in the Lasso of Truth, he saw that nuclear war would leave him without worshippers and called it off. Diana needed recovery afterward (vol. 2 #7).
New 52 continuity only; Hades takes him.

weaknesses: Lasso of Truth has subdued him more than once
Power depends on conflict, and Olympian power depends on belief
Magical weapons such as Grail's Godkiller sword can affect him
unknowns: The infobox lists time manipulation, mind control and illusion casting with no sourced feat in this pass; they are not counted as confirmed techniques.
The post-Crisis battle-axe defeat by Diana has no issue number in the cited page.

sources.supports: Powers list, limitations (magic weapons, Lasso, belief and conflict dependence), post-Crisis God of the Dead, New 52 vol. 4 #23 death, Rebirth imprisonment and Godkiller sword, continuity differences
Wonder Woman vol. 2 #6 synopsis: gods and Amazons near death from Ares' growing strength; Lasso shows him his plan's outcome; he ends the nuclear threat
Wonder Woman #6 'Powerplay', Jul 1987: Diana confronts Ares and uses the Lasso of Truth
Publisher profile: warmongering, godlike strength, combat strategy, weapons expert, immortality, combat skill

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics, Green Lantern vol. 4 (from #25, 2008) through Red Lanterns (2011-15) and Green Lanterns (Rebirth)
characters.summary: Founder of the Red Lantern Corps. His rage ring makes him a strong, durable flyer whose red energy can corrupt other Lanterns' rings, and unlike most Red Lanterns he keeps his full intellect. He also uses blood-magic divination.

techniques: red ring energy blasts and constructs (constructs learned during Blackest Night)
rage-tainted blood expelled through the mouth
red energy that corrupts and can burn away other rings' auras
blood rituals for divination and tracking

conditional.ability: Ring powers (blasts, constructs, flight, aura corruption)
conditional.dependsOn: Wearing a red power ring; he lost it to Guy Gardner in Red Lanterns #34

feats.claim: Threw a 14+ ton construction digger and shrugged off knife attacks.
Escaped Ysmault and mortally wounded Abin Sur.
Crucified Sinestro on Ysmault.
Resisted the Spectre's attempt to use his rage.
Stopped the Butcher from possessing him and locked it in his battery.

notableResults.note: Stopped and captured while hunting William Hand.
The cited page records the battle but not a clear winner.
Lost his ring and command of the Corps; regained control in Green Lanterns #1.

weaknesses: Blue Lantern energy can purify red corruption
Most of his arsenal depends on the ring
unknowns: The infobox lists blood portals, mind reading and rage absorption with no explanation in the cited page; they are not counted as confirmed techniques.
Whether he ever personally killed a Guardian is not supported by the cited page.

sources.supports: Ring nature, strength and durability (GL #31), constructs, rituals, intellect (GL #33), ring limitations (Red Lanterns #1, #3), aura corruption (GL #36), blue purification, fight history by issue
Red Lantern Corps origin: Atrocitus accessed the red light of rage through blood magic

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics from Batman: Vengeance of Bane #1 (1993)
characters.summary: A genius tactician from Peña Duro prison who breaks opponents physically and mentally. Venom pumped into his brain gives him superhuman strength, toughness and healing; cut the tubes and he crashes into withdrawal.

techniques: Venom-boosted grappling and strikes, including the backbreaker
long-term attrition strategy (wearing a target down before engaging)

conditional.ability: Superhuman strength, speed, durability and healing (about 15 tonnes of lift per the cited page)
conditional.dependsOn: Venom fed through tubes into his brain, usually from a dosing tank; he swore off it in Vengeance of Bane II (1995) and later used it again in Secret Six

feats.claim: Broke Batman's back after wearing him down during Knightfall.

notableResults.note: Batman was already exhausted when Bane attacked.

weaknesses: Venom dependence: doses about every 12 hours
Severe withdrawal if the supply is cut; the tubes are an exposed target
unknowns: How strong Bane is without Venom in exact terms is not sourced.

sources.supports: Venom effects and delivery, 15-tonne lift, intellect and languages, dosing interval and withdrawal, Azrael cutting the tubes, Batman #497, Detective Comics #701, Superman/Batman #53-56, swearing off Venom (1995) and relapse in Secret Six
Batman was exhausted when Bane broke him over his knee in Batman #497

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics: Batgirl 1967-1988, Oracle 1989-2011 (paraplegic after The Killing Joke), Batgirl again from the New 52 (2011). This record is for the active Batgirl identity; Oracle-era mobility limits do not apply to it.
characters.summary: A black-belt martial artist, eidetic-memory genius and elite hacker. She fights at a trained-human level and her bigger edge is information and coordination.

techniques: judo, karate and taekwondo (black belts before becoming Batgirl)
batarangs and small firearms (practiced after her paralysis)
offense.range: melee; thrown weapons at short range

support: Ran the Birds of Prey as head of operations
Coordinated hero counterstrikes as Oracle (Infinite Crisis, 2005)

feats.claim: Foiled Killer Moth's attempted kidnapping of Bruce Wayne in her debut.
Defeated the Calculator in Hong Kong and made his Anti-Life Equation fragments useless.

notableResults.note: Shot through the spine in an ambush, not a fight.

weaknesses: No superpowers
Ordinary human durability
unknowns: No sourced one-on-one wins against superpowered opponents.

sources.supports: Abilities (eidetic memory, hacking, black belts, eskrima, batarangs, firearms), Detective Comics #359, The Killing Joke, Oracle debut, New 52 restored mobility, Oracle: The Cure, Infinite Crisis coordination
Barbara Gordon as Batgirl and as Oracle with a photographic memory and hacking skills

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics Bruce Wayne from Detective Comics #27 (1939). Excludes Elseworlds (Red Son, The Dark Knight Returns) and one-off powered or armored states.
characters.summary: No powers: a master of virtually every martial art, a genius detective and tactician with near-limitless technology. Against superpowered foes he wins through preparation, weaknesses and gadgets, and he is still an ordinary human when hit.

techniques: gadgets and vehicles from the Wayne fortune
offense.range: melee to short range; vehicles extend reach

mechanisms: preparation, evasion and protective equipment (details vary by story)

conditional.dependsOn: Carrying it, e.g. the Kryptonite ring in Batman: Hush

conditional.ability: Counters to specific Justice League members
conditional.dependsOn: Prepared contingency plans (JLA: Tower of Babel, 2000)

feats.claim: His contingency plans, stolen by Ra's al Ghul, neutralized the Justice League.
With Catwoman, fought a Poison Ivy-controlled Superman and used the Kryptonite ring.

weaknesses: Ordinary human durability
Effectiveness against superpowered foes depends on equipment and preparation
unknowns: Exact issue numbers for the Hush Superman fight were not confirmed in this pass.

sources.supports: Publisher profile: no metahuman abilities; master of virtually every martial art; tactician; genius forensic scientist; advanced technology
Batman #497 back-breaking and Detective Comics #701 single-combat win over Bane
JLA: Tower of Babel: Ra's al Ghul used Batman's own plans against the Justice League
Batman: Hush fight with Superman using the Kryptonite ring from his utility belt
